output.summary: An erect wetland hybrid originating from broad-leaved and narrow-leaved cattails, it is abundant in the upper Midwestern United States, where its parents hybridize. It has long, swordlike leaves and velvety brown flower spikes, and can spread rapidly into dense stands that displace other plants.
output.edibilityNote: Rhizomes and pollen were eaten historically by Indigenous Americans and Europeans; contaminated water can make them dangerous because the plant accumulates metals and other toxins.
